author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking changes. The PR explicitly marks 'This PR does not introduce breaking changes.' The change makes no_progress_timeout default from 60 to 0, but the comment says '0 uses the default timeout', so it is a more conservative default that only changes behavior for callers relying on the old hardcoded 60-second stall timeout. The low_speed_time change in model_manager.cpp sets it to HttpClient::get_default_timeout() instead of 60 — this is an internal default adjustment, not a config or CLI change. All other HttpClient calls already use effective_timeout(), so this brings the download path into alignment.
evidence.documentation: The header comment on no_progress_timeout in http_client.h was updated to '0 uses the default timeout'. No external documentation changes are needed for this internal consistency fix. The change is not user-visible at the config or CLI level.
evidence.manual_release_testing: No evidence of manual testing. The change affects download timeout behavior that users can reach through model downloads. The PR description mentions the real-world trigger (Devlab Dispatch's Hugging Face proxy cold-start on 124 GB Halogen checkpoints dropping after 60 s, referenced in #3712), which is a credible user scenario, but no human explicitly tested this fix against a stalled or throttled download.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. The single commit aedbb4c2e737de6486fd90fe66b1182531417fcc was the only commit on the PR, approved by both reviewers, and no commits were added after either the first or latest approval.
evidence.review: Two approvals received: @Geramy ('Love this PR it's so simple, this is a what 5 line bug fix?') at 2026-10-01T19:07:12Z and @superm1 (empty) at 2026-10-02T17:56:29Z, both on commit aedbb4c2e737de6486fd90fe66b1182531417fcc. @abn is listed in docs/dev/contribute.md as the maintainer with HTTP/sockets expertise but did not review. The PR author (@jeremyfowers) is also the admin maintainer responsible for CI, which makes self-approval somewhat less rigorous.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change only adjusts timeout values and an error message string. It does not introduce network calls, credential handling, code execution paths, or permission changes.
evidence.tests: No new tests were added. The change modifies default timeout values and an error message string — not a new feature or algorithm. All CI checks passed: C++ Server Build + Test (amd64 + arm64), docker-smoke-test, CMake build + MCP smoke test, Server download registry tests, CodeQL (all languages), Build and smoke test on multiple platforms, packaging builds, and all embeddable builds. The existing C++ unit tests and download registry tests cover the HTTP client at a higher level but do not exercise the specific stall timeout path with a simulated slow download.

maintainer_todos.text: Start the server, configure a very long global_timeout, and download a large model from a slow or flaky endpoint to confirm the download does not abort prematurely at 60 seconds but respects the global_timeout value.

subject: fix(http): make download stall timeouts follow global_timeout (#3730)
summary: Makes download stall timeouts (no_progress_timeout defaulting to global_timeout, and low_speed_time for model manifest downloads defaulting to global_timeout) consistent with every other HttpClient call, and fixes the stall error message to report the actual timeout that fired.
verdict_reason: The HTTP subject-area specialist (@abn) did not review this HTTP-internal change, and no manual testing evidence exists for the download stall timeout behavior that users can reach.
